answer: Memory-hard epoch challenges resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to compute an Argon2 proof seeded by a fresh DAG vertex within a tight deadline before peers accept requests. Because concurrent proofs cannot reuse memory banks before the window closes, attackers cannot spread clones across an idle CPU meadow and hit a hard reef of DRAM capacity per identity. However, strict RAM bursts exclude lightweight edge devices and favor bulk hardware farms.
